As per the facts of the case on 11.03.2014, at about 06.20 AM , the petitioner alongwith her family members were going, in a car, from her house to Sadar Bazar Delhi.

And when they reached at main road Deenpur opposite Dispensary New Delhi,
suddenly a car bearing No. DL1LE8126 being driven by its driver came at a very high speed, in rash and negligent manner and hit their car from right side.
As a result of which petitioner and other occupants of the car received injuries .
The petitioner was taken to R.T.R.M Hospital , New Delhi.
She has suffered injuries in her left Femur due to this accident.
The injuries opined as grievous in nature.

2. The present application/claim petition has been filed contending that said accident took place, due to rash and negligent driving by (respondent no.3/ Driver) who was driving Vehicle No. DL 1LE8126.
The offending vehicle was owned by Sushil Bohra ( respondent no.1/owner) and was insured with M/S IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Co Ltd (respondent no.2).

3. The respondent No.1 has filed reply/WS stating therein that a false case been filed against him to extort money from him.
It is stated that alleged accident pertains to some other incident in which petitioner might have been involved.
4. The respondent No.3 has not appeared in this case.

5. The respondent no. 2, Insurance company has filed its reply stating therein that insurance company is not liable to pay compensation amount as the offending vehicle was not insured with IFFCO Tokio General Insurance.

sentences.text: The proof of negligence while disposing of a claim application under MACT, is not that strict as it is for the offence under Section 279/337/338 of IPC.
It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that victim's car driver was at fault, in any way.
12.The fact that petitioner suffered injuries in that accident is also supported by the medical documents Ex PW1/2.
After investigation, police has also indicted respondent no. 1 as an accused for the offences punishable under Sections 279/337/338 IPC.
The case has been registered against respondent no. 3.
The fact of accident and the respondent no.3 is facing the trial as an accused is not disputed.

Considering all these facts, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of a car bearing No.DL1LE8126 by respondent no. 3 thereby causing injuries to the petitioner.
ISSUE No.2: ? Whether the petitioner in the above mentioned case is entitled to claim compensation , if so , what amount and from whom?
Being injured, petitioner is well within her rights to claim compensation.
It is there on record, as per the deposition of PW 2 and the discharged card Ex Mark C.
The petitioner was removed to RTRM Hospital for her treatment.

It is deposed by (PW2) that due to the said accident, she herself and her family MACT No. 1092/16 Gun vs Sushil Bohra & ors Page No. 9 of 14 members have suffered great mental pain, agony, love and affection, and loss of social activities etc.

sentences.text: The next point that is to be discussed is pain and suffering and to calculate the same, the nature of injuries caused to the injured due to the accident, duration for which she got medical treatment and she was constrained to live in bed are few factors which must be taken into account.
After the accident, petitioner was taken to RTRM Hospital New Delhi.
It is very much apparent that when a person is leading a normal life suddenly meets with an accident which changes his complete life, the mental agony which she faces cannot be considered.

The whole life changes and everything looks darker to that person which can be beyond out of imagination, such a scenario MACT No. 1092/16 Gun vs Sushil Bohra & ors Page No. 10 of 14 could shake even braver of bravest.

sentences.text: The physical pain which petitioner had undergone after the accident cannot be explained as to a miserable person every body sympathizes though it never pacifies a victim.

To compensate petitioner under this head,
a sum of Rs.50,000/ is awarded to her.

Mental and physical shock:
18.

The petitioner was infant child of one year of age at the time of accident but due to this mis happening with her, all her dreams and expectations got completely shattered which cannot be compensated in monetary terms.
However, to console her to an extent, a sum of Rs.25,000/ is awarded to petitioner under this head.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The proof of negligence while disposing of a claim application under MACT, is not that strict as it is for the offence under Section 279/337/338 of IPC.
It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that victim's car driver was at fault, in any way.
Considering all these facts, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of a car bearing No.DL1LE8126 by respondent no. 3 thereby causing injuries to the petitioner.
The next point that is to be discussed is pain and suffering and to calculate the same, the nature of injuries caused to the injured due to the accident, duration for which she got medical treatment and she was constrained to live in bed are few factors which must be taken into account.
After the accident, petitioner was taken to RTRM Hospital New Delhi.
It is very much apparent that when a person is leading a normal life suddenly meets with an accident which changes his complete life, the mental agony which she faces cannot be considered.
The whole life changes and everything looks darker to that person which can be beyond out of imagination, such a scenario MACT No. 1092/16 Gun vs Sushil Bohra & ors Page No. 10 of 14 could shake even braver of bravest.
The physical pain which petitioner had undergone after the accident cannot be explained as to a miserable person every body sympathizes though it never pacifies a victim.
To compensate petitioner under this head,
a sum of Rs.50,000/ is awarded to her.
Mental and physical shock:
18.
The petitioner was infant child of one year of age at the time of accident but due to this mis happening with her, all her dreams and expectations got completely shattered which cannot be compensated in monetary terms.
This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioner and against respondent by holding that accident in question took place due to rash or negligent driving of Car bearing No.DL1LE8126 being driven by respondent no.3 and petitioner suffered injuries in that accident and petitioner is entitled for compensation.
It is submitted that offending vehicle is not insured with MACT No. 1092/16 Gun vs Sushil Bohra & ors Page No. 11 of 14 IFFCO Tokio General Insurance company Ltd at the time of accident.
IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Company Ltd.
Reliance is placed on ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Ltd Vs Ashokan &
Ors C.M.A No. 275 of 2016 and CMP No.2312 of 2016 of Hon'ble Madras High Court and Shriram General Insurance Company Ltd Vs Arvind Dattatray Shindode, First Appeal N0. 55 of 2023 of Hon'ble Bombay High Court.

24. This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioner and against respondent No.1 and 3 by holding that petitioner is entitled for compensation from respondent 1 and 3.

25.

26. Considering that petitioner is a minor hence the entire amount of compensation be kept in the form of FDR in the name of petitioner for the period from one year to eight year with cumulative interest.

27. The salient features as prescribed in the judgment in Rajesh Tyagi Vs. Ramesh Chandra Gupta FAO No. 842/2009 and MAC. App. No. 422/2009 decided on 07.11.2014 are to be applied:
(i) Original fixed deposit receipt be retained by the bank in safe custody.
However, the original passbook shall be given to the claimant along with the photocopy of the FDR.
(ii) The original fixed deposit receipt be handed over to the claimant at the end of the fixed deposit period.
(iii) Photo identity card shall be issued to the claimant and the withdrawal shall be permitted only after due verification by the Bank of the identity card of the claimant.
MACT No. 1092/16 Gun vs Sushil Bohra & ors Page No. 13 of 14 (iv) No cheque book/ATM/debit card/credit card shall be issued to the claimant without permission of the Court.
(v) No loan, advance or withdrawal or premature encashment shall be allowed on the fixed deposit without permission of the Court 28.
Respondent no..1 and 3 directed to deposit entire amount of compensation with this tribunal,
within 30 days from today, with advance notice to petitioner.
